hypothesis: The sole observed T3 program was correct and measured 6.49 µs on average versus the baseline's 47.08 µs, but the catalog has only one distinct T3 program and provides no matched atomic-versus-control result. This contrasting candidate tests a warp-level CTA reduction with 256-, 1024-, and 4096-element tiles. The atomic path includes default-stream memset plus one atomicAdd per CTA; the non-atomic path uses the same 1024-element first-pass mapping and a second finalization kernel. The broad size dispatch is for whole-call comparison, not a prediction that atomics win.
notes: The atomic branch performs cudaMemsetAsync and then launches its tiled kernel on the default stream. The control overwrites every scratch partial and finalizes only those partials, so it does not depend on stale scratch. Both tiled modes use the same 1024-element first-pass mapping; their dispatch ranges differ, so the controller's repeated whole-call results should not be interpreted as a same-input A/B measurement. Small inputs retain the original reduction path.
transformations: Kept the original 128-thread multi-pass reducer for n < 4096 and added explicit handling for nonpositive n and n == 1.
Added a 256-thread CTA reduction using warp-level reduction and shared storage for one partial per warp, replacing per-level CTA-wide synchronization in the tiled path.
Added 256-, 1024-, and 4096-element CTA tile configurations; each CTA contributes one sum through atomicAdd in the atomic path.
